title: Fire & Smoke Mitigation Late Fee Policy
content:
> The job must be in invoiced status when a late fee is charged. A late fee may post only after the grace period following the payment due date recorded at invoicing has fully passed. The grace period is counted in calendar days starting the day after the payment due date, and the first late fee may post on the day after the grace period's last day. A late fee is assessed at most once per calendar month fee period at the late fee percentage of the balance due, with the late fee minimum as a floor, rounded to the cent, half up. No late fee posts on an insurance-claim job while its linked claim file is in opened, estimate submitted or approved status and the suspension period counted from the invoice date has not ended. Late fees are never back-dated to a suspended period.

This policy governs late fees on past-due Fire & Smoke Mitigation balances: the status in which they may be charged, the grace period, the monthly amount, and the suspension while an insurance claim is pending.

## Status

A late fee is charged only on a job in invoiced status.

## Grace period

The grace period follows the payment due date recorded at invoicing. It is counted in calendar days starting the day after the payment due date, and the first late fee may post on the day after the grace period's last day. A late fee may not post on any day of the grace period, the last day included.

| Day, relative to the payment due date | May a late fee post? |
|---|---|
| The due date itself | no |
| Any day inside the grace period, its last day included | no |
| The day after the grace period's last day | yes, this is the first day a late fee may post |

Hypothetical calendar: a payment due date of 10 May with a hypothetical grace period of 5 calendar days gives grace days of 11, 12, 13, 14 and 15 May. No late fee posts on 15 May; the first late fee may post on 16 May.

## Amount and frequency

A late fee is assessed at most once per calendar month fee period. Its amount is the tier's late fee percentage of the balance due, rounded to the cent, half up, and never less than the tier's late fee minimum, which acts as a floor.

Hypothetical figures, using a hypothetical 2 percent and a hypothetical minimum of 30.00:

| Balance due | Percentage of the balance, rounded half up | Against the floor of 30.00 | Late fee |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1234.25 | 24.685, rounded to 24.69 | below the floor | 30.00 |
| 2000.25 | 40.005, rounded to 40.01 | above the floor | 40.01 |

A second late fee in the same calendar month fee period is not assessed.

## Suspension while a claim is pending

No late fee posts on an insurance-claim job while its linked claim file is in opened, estimate submitted or approved status and the suspension period counted from the invoice date has not ended. The suspension period is the tier's claim-pending suspension period.

| Job funded under an insurance claim | Linked claim file in opened, estimate submitted or approved status | Suspension period from the invoice date not yet ended | Suspension |
|---|---|---|---|
| yes | yes | yes | applies: no late fee posts |
| yes | yes | no | does not apply |
| yes | no | yes | does not apply |
| no (self-pay) | not applicable | yes or no | does not apply |

Where the suspension does not apply, the status, grace period and once-per-month conditions above still govern whether a late fee may post.

Late fees are never back-dated to a suspended period: a fee period that fell inside the suspension takes no late fee after the suspension ends.
